overview: This assessment is Unit Assessment Task 1 (UAT 1) — Unit Knowledge Test for SITHPAT018 Produce chocolate confectionery. It assesses the knowledge you need to temper couverture and produce individual chocolates in a commercial patisserie.
The unit sits within SIT40721 Certificate IV in Patisserie (AQF Level 4). Your answers must therefore explain your knowledge and apply it to workplace situations, not simply repeat definitions.

Every question is set at La Meridienne Patisserie, Rundle Street, Adelaide, a patisserie and chocolatier producing a boxed retail range and function orders. Appendix A sets out the chocolate range and Appendix B the couverture specification. Read both before you begin and use them wherever a question refers to them.

whatThisCovers.intro: The questions are grouped into six sections that map directly to the unit's Knowledge Evidence:

sections.text: Section A — culinary terms and trade names, date codes and rotation labels, and indicators of ingredient freshness and quality.
Section B — the processes used to produce different types of chocolates, and the historical and cultural origins of a variety of chocolates.
Section C — mise en place requirements, safe operational practices for equipment, and protection of polished chocolate moulds.
Section D — tempering methods, melting and tempering temperatures, the properties of tempered couverture and the expected characteristics of solidified couverture.
Section E — the characteristics of centres and fillings, methods of coating centres, and the complementary tastes and textures of dark, milk and white couverture.
Section F — decoration techniques, and the environmental conditions for storing ingredients and finished chocolates.

howYouAreAssessed: Each question is marked Satisfactory (S) or Not Satisfactory (NS). All questions must be Satisfactory for this task to be judged Satisfactory.
You must complete every assessment task for the unit before your assessor records an overall result of Competent (C) or Not Yet Competent (NYC). Practical skills are assessed separately in UAT 2.
instructions: Read each task carefully and complete every item in your own words.
Use the South Australian legislation, codes, standards and authorities that apply.
Type your answers where possible; handwritten work must be neat and legible.
If you have a learning need, you may request a reasonable adjustment before you begin.
Answer all fifteen questions and every part of each question. Every part has its own writing space directly beneath it.
Follow the word guide shown in the Maps to box for each question; it indicates the depth of answer expected.
Answer in your own words. Copied work cannot be assessed and will be recorded as Not Satisfactory.
Where a question refers to La Meridienne Patisserie, answer in that workplace context, using Appendix A and Appendix B where the question directs you to them.

rulesOfEvidence.intro: Your assessor applies the four rules of evidence to the work you submit. The table explains what each rule means for this task.
headers: What it means for this assessment
rows: Your answers address the knowledge required by SITHPAT018 and show that you can apply it to chocolate production in a commercial patisserie.
You answer every question and every part, at the depth indicated by the word guide, with enough detail for your assessor to judge your knowledge.
The work is your own, produced under supervision without generative AI. Answers written in your own words, referring to your own practice, demonstrate authenticity.
Your answers reflect current industry practice and the legislation, codes and standards that apply in South Australia now.

qualityExpected: Write in complete sentences and use correct culinary and patisserie terminology. Where a word guide is given, treat it as the depth expected rather than a strict limit.
Where a question asks you to explain, give the reason as well as the fact. Where it asks you to apply, refer to the scenario, the product or the equipment concerned.

Your assessor marks your work against the benchmark answers held in the separate assessor marking guide for this unit, together with the Knowledge Evidence mapping matrix included at the end of this learner task.

paragraphs: This assessment is open book. You may use your learner resource, standard recipes, manufacturer instructions, Appendix A, Appendix B and the college's food safety program while you work.
You will complete the assessment individually and under assessor supervision, in a classroom or in the college's simulated commercial patisserie.

assessmentConditions.heading: Duration and session structure
paragraphs: This task is completed in two supervised sessions of up to five hours each. Your assessor will confirm the session dates and the due date recorded on the cover sheet.

assessmentConditions.heading: Security between sessions
paragraphs: Your assessor collects all question papers, responses and working notes at the end of each session and stores them securely. You must not retain copies of completed responses or of the assessment questions between sessions, and you must not discuss the questions with other learners at any time.

assessmentConditions.heading: Individual work, permitted assistance and generative AI
paragraphs: All answers must be your own work, written in your own words. You may ask your assessor to clarify what a question is asking, and you may use the resources listed below. You must not work with another learner on any response, or copy from another learner's work.

Generative AI must not draft, generate, paraphrase or substantially rewrite any assessment response. Basic spelling and grammar tools, and approved accessibility tools, may be used. Any approved assistive technology must be declared to your assessor before you begin.

assessmentConditions.heading: Assessment mode
paragraphs: Where the cover sheet records this task as Online, it may be completed only in an approved live-supervised session with identity verification and secure submission. Unsupervised online or take-home completion is not permitted for this task.

appendixA.title: Appendix A — La Meridienne chocolate range
appendixA.intro: This is the current boxed range produced at La Meridienne Patisserie, Rundle Street, Adelaide. Products A1 to A10 all correspond to recipes in your SITHPAT018 Recipe Workbook. A9 and A10 provide the enrobing and prepared hollow-shell processes required across the range. Where a question asks you to select a product, select only from this range. Do not invent a product.
rows: A1 — Rocher / mendiant, fruit and nut
Hard centre — fruit and nut cluster
Rough surface, fruit and nut set on top
A2 — Chocolate heaven bliss ball, marzipan

appendixB.title: Appendix B — MVC tempering standard
appendixB.intro: These are the tempering parameters taught in your SITHPAT018 Recipe Workbook and used for all products made at La Meridienne. The workbook tempers couverture by the vaccination (addition) method: the couverture is melted, then unmelted seed couverture is added and stirred until the temperature falls to the working temperature below.
appendixB.afterTable: If the couverture cools to 27 °C and is still fluid, it can be reheated to a working consistency. If it has cooled and solidified, it must be re-tempered. Follow this standard for all La Meridienne products.
productionData: The tempering machine cools melted couverture at an average of 1.5 °C per minute.
Where the vaccination (addition) method is used, seed couverture is reserved from the total weight of couverture required, not added on top of it.
Raspberry jelly for the A9 square requires four hours to set before it can be cut. Caramel for the A3 bonbon requires two hours to cool before it can be piped.
Only one tempering machine, one enrobing machine and one set of polished bonbon moulds are available.

foundationSkills.heading: Foundation skills
paragraphs: Numeracy — the unit requires numeracy skills to determine tempering times and temperatures. This is evidenced in Question 9, where you state working temperatures from the couverture specification and calculate the time required to bring melted couverture down to its working temperature.

Reading and writing — the unit's descriptors require locating information in standard recipes and on date code and stock rotation labels, and recording clear sequenced instructions for new recipes with ingredient quantities. These are assessed in UAT 2, where you work from live recipes, labels and stock, and are not claimed as directly evidenced by this written task.
